request.state:
Target: Apple (AAPL). Apple develops and sells personal computing devices including iPhone, Mac and iPad, with operating systems and digital services.

Focal announcement: Apple reports third quarter results.

Decision cutoff: 2024-08-01T23:59:59-04:00. Only information available before this cutoff is admissible.

Source: Apple reports third quarter results. Published: 2024-08-01. URL: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2024/08/apple-reports-third-quarter-results.

Condensed source facts; other details are omitted: CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced financial results for its fiscal 2024 third quarter ended June 29, 2024. The Company posted quarterly revenue of $85.8 billion, up 5 percent year over year, and quarterly earnings per diluted share of $1.40, up 11 percent year over year. “Today Apple is reporting a new June quarter revenue record of $85.8 billion, up 5 percent from a year ago,” said Tim Cook, Apple’s CEO. “During the quarter, our record business performance generated EPS growth of 11 percent and nearly $29 billion in operating cash flow, allowing us to return over $32 billion to shareholders,” said Luca Maestri, Apple’s CFO. Apple’s board of directors has declared a cash dividend of $0.25 per share of the Company’s common stock.

The exact historical text version is unverified. This is an incomplete source-based reconstruction.

Expectations: No point-in-time analyst consensus or market-implied expectation is available.

No company-wide comparable financial baselines or incremental magnitude inputs were supplied. Do not infer that a large headline amount is material to the target.

The stock showed a substantial past decline over the latest completed session, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The stock showed a very small past rise over the recent trading week, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The stock showed a very small past decline over the recent trading month, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The stock's recent daily variability was moderate. Variability describes the size of ordinary fluctuations, not their future direction.

The broad market (SPY) showed a substantial past decline over the latest completed session, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The broad market (SPY) showed a modest past rise over the recent trading week, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The broad market (SPY) showed a modest past decline over the recent trading month, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The broad market (SPY)'s recent daily variability was relatively subdued. Variability describes the size of ordinary fluctuations, not their future direction.

Over the recent trading week, the stock showed very small underperformance relative to the broad market.

Over the recent trading month, the stock showed very small outperformance relative to the broad market.

These are coarse descriptions computed from observed historical inputs. Strong past movement or relative strength is not evidence that the next return must continue or reverse.

The previously fitted market-only reference model favored an upward return beyond the neutral band. Its leading outcome was favored, with meaningful uncertainty. It still assigned meaningful possibility to a return inside the narrow neutral band and a downward return beyond the neutral band. This is a training-only model forecast, not an observed outcome or independent news evidence.

The neutral return band's half-width is narrower than the code-computed ordinary five-session variability scale. An irrelevant article does not eliminate ordinary price movement; this is not a calculated class probability.

Forecast target: entry is the first regular-session open after the cutoff; exit is the fifth session close, counting entry as session one. Raw return above +1% is up; within inclusive -1% to +1% is flat; below -1% is down. The initial pre-entry reaction is outside this target.

Do not invent analyst consensus, incremental target sales, new corporate cash payments, or an already-priced news reaction.
